qs.situation: Rohan's shop promises delivery 'in 3 business days'. An order is placed on Monday, and Wednesday is a national public holiday.
options: Only Saturdays and Sundays are days off, so the holiday counts as a working day and delivery is Thursday
National public holidays are also skipped, so delivery is Friday
Our own shop-closure days are skipped too, so delivery date follows our own holiday calendar

qs.situation: A customer pays with a 16-digit card, and the receipt must hide most of the number.
options: Only the last 4 digits are visible
The first 6 and last 4 digits are visible
Only the last 2 digits are visible

qs.situation: Priya's invoice of ₹10,000 is 45 days overdue.
options: 1.5% of the amount for each 30-day month late, so ₹150 per month, charged in proportion to the days
One flat fee of ₹500, however late it is
₹50 for every day late

qs.situation: An invoice of ₹1,000 stays unpaid for 3 years and the late fee keeps growing.
options: The fee can never be more than the invoice itself (₹1,000)
The fee stops at 25% of the invoice (₹250)
No limit; the fee keeps growing for as long as it is unpaid

qs.situation: A staff member's badge is printed for 'Mary Jane Watson'.
options: MW, the first and last name only
MJW, one letter for every name
MJ, the first two names only

qs.situation: On the dashboard, last month's sales were ₹0 and this month's are ₹5,000.
options: Show nothing (no percentage), because the change can't be worked out
Show 100% growth
Show a fixed label such as 'New' instead of a number

qs.situation: A customer gives their phone number as '(415) 555-0132 ext. 45'.
options: Save the number and drop the extension
Refuse to save it, so staff must ask for a clean number
Save the number and keep the extension separately

qs.situation: A customer in London enters the number +44 20 7946 0958.
options: Leave it blank, since only US numbers are supported
Keep the number as typed, with the plus sign and digits only
Flag it as invalid so staff must fix it

qs.situation: How should the shipping price be built for a parcel going to zone 3?
options: A base charge plus a rate per kilo, with each farther zone costing more
One flat price per zone, whatever the weight
A price for each weight band (for example up to 1 kg, 1 to 5 kg, over 5 kg) in each zone

qs.situation: A parcel weighs exactly 2 kg, and another weighs 2.1 kg.
options: Any started kilo is charged, so 2 kg pays for 2 kilos and 2.1 kg pays for 3 kilos
Charged by the exact weight, so 2.1 kg pays slightly more than 2 kg
Rounded up to the next half kilo, so 2.1 kg pays for 2.5 kilos

qs.situation: A customer wants to send an 80 kg crate to zone 2.
options: Charge normally, with the price rising with weight
Refuse it, because it is over our parcel limit
Use a special flat heavy-freight price

qs.situation: A customer ships a tiny 50 g parcel to zone 1.
options: They pay the full base charge, so there is a minimum
They pay a reduced price in proportion to the weight
It ships free

qs.situation: A product's average rating is 4.3 out of 5.
options: Shown to the nearest half star, so 4.5 stars
Shown to the nearest whole star, so 4 stars
Always rounded down, so 4 stars

qs.situation: A brand-new product has no reviews yet.
options: Show 'No reviews yet' instead of stars
Show five empty stars
Show nothing at all

qs.situation: A blog post has a very long title of about 120 characters.
options: The web address uses the whole title, with no cut-off
The web address is cut at 60 characters
The web address is cut at about 80 characters, at the end of a whole word
